niche.habitat: Alpine slopes, dark lava tubes, forest canopies, and night-active zones.
niche.diet: Carnivore/omnivore; small vertebrates, birds, insects, and carrion.
niche.active: Nocturnal and crepuscular; avoids daytime UV and heat.

body: Oversized pupils and a reflective tapetum capture photons in moonlit or starlit dark, while broad tympanic membranes isolate prey movements through dense fog and wind. Ventral photophores pulse rhythmically for silent intraspecific communication, and melanin-rich shields protect against nocturnal UV reflection and temperature swings.

chains.trait: Oversized pupils and reflective tapetum layer
links: Shift activity to the empty night niche

skill.effect: See 3× farther in moonlight; −50% sight in full sun

chains.weakness: A flare or bright sun blinds it for 5 s; fight at noon.

journal.en: The dark is a country with room.

plausibility.summary: State that Night eyes is strongest on moonless nights (F6) and modest on full-moon nights; tapetum adds eyeshine cost (predators/observers) and slightly lowers diurnal acuity, not only a flat −50% sun penalty.

temperament: Stealthy and observant, using darkness and low-frequency sound to ambush or evade.
moments: Moonlight bleaches the snowline; the creature drops from a basalt ledge, silent on padded feet. A low-frequency thrum vibrates through the tuff as it locates a burrow. The ventral lights flash once—acknowledgment, not warning.
